key_insight: PHO-Agents combines structured EHR modeling with multi-agent LLM reasoning to improve health outcome prediction and generate more interpretable explanations.
clinical_relevance: This hybrid system could support clinical decision-making by predicting patient risks more accurately while grounding outputs in external medical evidence.
method: Encoded longitudinal EHR data to create patient representations and initial prediction logits.
Converted EHR outputs into patient summaries for a data agent.
Used retrieval plus research, doctor, and leader agents to review evidence and synthesize final predictions and explanations; fused these with the EHR model output.
evidence_signal: Evaluated on three real-world cohorts (AKI mortality, CKD-to-AKI onset, and ICI-related adverse events) and outperformed single-agent and multi-agent LLM baselines, including PR-AUC 90.20 ± 2.07 vs 56.46 ± 2.98 in AKI mortality.
watch_item: The approach depends on reliable retrieval, LLM reasoning, and site-specific EHR data quality, so real-world deployment may require careful validation and oversight.
paper_title: PHO-Agents: A Large Language Model Powered Multi-Agent System for Predicting Health Outcomes
